newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-German, U.S groups join W. Australia DRI rush.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-German, U.S groups join W. Australia DRI rush.

text.p: German industrial conglomerate Metallgesellshaft GmbH (MG) and El Paso Energy Corp of the United States have joined the rush into integrated iron ore projects in Western Australia with a A$750 million plant planned for the Mt Gibson area.

MG, through a wholly owned subsidiary Lurgi (Australia) Pty Ltd, and El Paso Energy, through Brisbane-based Epic Energy Pty Ltd, have become minority shareholders in the company earmarked to manage the project, Mt Gibson Iron NL.
Australian Securities Commission (ASC) documents show publicly listed Energy Equity Corp Ltd and infrastructure investor Infratil Australia Ltd, have joined MGI's share register.
MGI's parent company and other shareholder is unlisted Resource Equities Ltd, whose chairman Brian Johnson was formerly with Portman Mining Ltd.
MGI directors include Johnson, John Brodziak, another former Portman executive, and Terrence Strapp, the chairman of investment banker Oakvale Capital Ltd.
The Mt Gibson Project is earmarked for Western Australia's mid-west region, the same area where Taiwan's An Feng (Australia) Pty Ltd plans to base its A$1.4 billion iron and steel project.

In contrast to the An Feng project, Mt Gibson has attracted virtually no public attention, despite the announcement late last year by South Korea's Halla Engineering and Construction Co Ltd that it had agreed to fund a feasibility study and take a 35 percent interest in the project if it proceeded.
Earlier this month, Western Australian Governor Michael Jeffery told state parliament that a State Agreement was being negotiated for Mt Gibson.
Resources Minister Colin Barnett told Reuters this week the project "has made wonderful advances". Mt Gibson Iron declined to comment when contacted by Reuters.
A search of ASC records showed A$2.45 million had been injected into MGI since it was incorporated on July 4 last year, through several share allotments.
Resource Equities Ltd has invested A$1.7 million, Infratil and MG have invested A$250,000 each while Energy Equity has invested $125,000 for 625,000 ordinary shares.

Brisbane-based Epic Energy Pty Ltd, which owns and operates Australian energy assets formerly owned by the U.S. group Tenneco Inc, also paid $125,000 for 625,000 shares. Epic Energy is owned 30 percent by El Paso Energy.
Most investments were made in the past two months, with MG, Epic Energy, Infratil and Energy Equity now equal one-fifth owners of MGI.
The Mt Gibson project aims to produce two million tonnes a year of direct reduced iron (DRI) and hot briquetted iron (HBI).
The iron ore deposit is about 320 km south east of Geraldton and about 430 kilometres north of Perth.
The ore is planned to be beneficiated before being transported by slurry pipeline to a DRI plant at Moonyoonooka, near Geraldton. The ore will then be pelletised before being converted to DRI/HBI.
MGI intends to complete a bankable feasibility study and obtain all of government approvals by October 1997, according to Barnett. The iron pellets will be exported to Asian steel mills.
Barnett told Reuters a Mt Gibson State Agreement was "still possibly some time off, maybe later this year". Mt Gibson was working to secure markets and finance, he said.
